Whether $325 is itself the 28/29 cap is UNVERIFIED at primary - primary pull owed (OPEN #12). The AT-CAP + 6,831 MW SHORT facts are unaffected, and WATT-01's HIT is robust under either reading (100% or 97.5%, both >= its registered 95% bar). Row kept as written; this annotation is the correction. || RESOLVED 2026-09-06 AT PRIMARY: PJM news release 2026-07-14 headline reads 'Capacity Price Comes in at the Cap of $325, Down 2.5%' - so $325 IS the 2028/29 FERC-approved cap and the auction cleared at 100% of it. column10: HIT 2026-09-02 (resolved 5 days early on the 9/7 date — and SEVEN WEEKS LATE against the fact). RESOLVED ON THE 202(c) LIMB, NOT THE POSTING LIMB. Criteria verbatim: '>=1 EEA2+ posting OR 202(c) order in PJM footprint by 9/7'. WHAT SATISFIES IT: DOE Order No. 202-26-41, issued 2026-09-01 to PJM Interconnection L.L.C. under FPA s202(c), effective 2026-09-01 through 11:59 PM ET 2026-09-08 - 'directs PJM to dispatch specified units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability' and 'authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3'. VERIFIED AT TWO INDEPENDENT PRIMARIES: (1) DOE CESER 2026 202(c) order index (energy.gov/ceser/2026-doe-202c-orders); (2) PJM Inside Lines 'Hot Weather Operations Update - Sept. 2, 2026', verbatim: 'PJM requested and received a combined emergency order... to be effective through Sept. 8, from the U.S. Department of Energy for temporary relief from environmental permit restrictions for generating units and/or to direct backup generation resources at large loads to operate'. THE POSTING LIMB DID NOT FIRE: PJM posted NERC EEA-1 twice (#105473 9/1 18:03, #105479 9/2 16:00) plus a Pre-Emergency Load Management Reduction Action (#105472, 9/1 17:15, AEP BGE COMED DOM PEPCO). EEA-1 IS NOT EEA2+. The disjunction needed only one limb; the 202(c) limb carried it. Recording BOTH facts so the grade is not later misread as an EEA2 event. *** IT WAS ALREADY A HIT ON 2026-07-14 AND I MISSED IT FOR SEVEN WEEKS. *** DOE Order No. 202-26-35 (issued 7/14, PJM, effective 7/14-7/21, 'dispatch units for reliability; backup generation at loads before/during EEA 3') ALSO satisfies the criteria and post-dates this prediction's 7/10 registration. On 7/22 I wrote 'the 7/15-16 EEA-1 is sub-EEA2 (near-miss, not banked)' - a CORRECT statement about the posting limb, applied as if it settled the whole prediction. The DOE order covering that same heat episode was one index page away and I never checked it, at any of four subsequent boots. ROOT CAUSE IS DOCUMENTATION, NOT RESEARCH: this registered row always carried both limbs. Every carry-forward SUMMARY of it dropped the second - STATUS said 'WATT-02 (9/7) - EEA2+ by Labor Day'; SCRATCH said 'its bar is a POSTING'; and the 2026-09-02 PROME task brief inherited that compression and restated it back to me as established fact ('its bar is a POSTING, not a price spike (your own note)'). FOUR derived surfaces carried a one-limb rule; the ledger was correct throughout. => GRADE AT THE REGISTERED ROW, NEVER AT THE SURFACE THAT QUOTES IT. [[finding_summary_section_merges_what_the_body_separates]] Logged L-39. NOTE THE MIGRATION: the compressed caveat is TRUE of the NEIGHBOURING prediction - WATT-06's criteria really is posting-only ('a Max Gen Emergency / Load Management Alert (EEA-1) or above, PJM-RTO region, effective 7/17-8/15, on emergencyprocedures.pjm.com'). A correct caveat migrated to the wrong prediction. WATT-06's MISS is UNAFFECTED and stands: 202-26-35 was issued 7/14, outside WATT-06's 7/17-8/15 window, and WATT-06's bar is a PJM posting, not a DOE order. registered if_falsified DOES NOT EXECUTE (it was written for a MISS). CONTENT OF THE HIT: the recurrence case is now n=3 episodes in one season - 7/3 (EEA2 + 202-26-32A/33A), 7/15-16 (EEA-1 + 202-26-35), 9/1-9/3+ (EEA-1 x2 + 202-26-41 + a dispatched load-management action) - and it SPANS JULY AND SEPTEMBER, so the 'heat-clustered, not a structural cadence' read that WATT-06's MISS correctly established FOR JULY does not extend across the season. A SUCCESSOR IS OWED once the current episode closes; deliberately NOT registered mid-episode.

column10: MISS 2026-08-17 (resolved 2d late — no boot 8/4->8/17). ZERO PJM-RTO emergency-class postings effective 7/17-8/15. The registered if_falsified branch EXECUTES: the two July episodes (7/3 EEA2, 7/15-16 EEA-1) were HEAT-CLUSTERED, not a structural cadence. RESOLVED ON THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS, because the PJM board retains only recent postings and cannot alone certify a 30-day window: (1) BOARD/ID-CONTINUITY — my dated 8/4 boot recorded 0 emergency-class 7/17-8/4 with #105429 (8/3) latest; today's board carries #105434 (8/6, routine FE-AP Post-Contingency Local Load Relief Warning) as the ONLY posting and the latest ID, so no posting of any class was issued 8/6-8/17; residual uncertainty is confined to IDs 105430-105433 (issued 8/3-8/6). (2) PHYSICAL — EIA-930 PJM hourly across the full window: max daily peak 149,871 MW (7/17T00Z, the tail of the 7/16 EEA-1 episode); the highest AUGUST day was 145,375 MW (8/6), ~14 GW BELOW the 159,046 MW at which the 7/15-16 EEA-1 fired and ~37 GW below PJM's ~182 GW capacity, so an EEA-1 inside the 8/3-8/6 residual is physically implausible. (3) PUBLISHER — PJM Inside Lines issued a HOT WEATHER ALERT for Aug 9-11 (forecast 136,029/146,541/144,018 MW) and states it is 'a routine procedure' that 'does not require any action from customers' — a PREPARATORY alert, explicitly NOT emergency-class, and PJM published no Max Gen / Load Management / EEA post in August. ⚠️ DOES NOT COUNT: the 8/16 DM2 RED-band price spike ($1,217.52 5-min) falls OUTSIDE this window (ends 8/15) AND is a price event, not a posting — WATT-06's bar is a POSTING. Banking it would be the unpassed-forecast trap in reverse. -> P1 already at 2 (re-scored 4->3->2 across 7/16-8/4), so the registered de-escalation is already executed and exceeded.

column10: HIT 2026-08-04 on the ABEYANCE BRANCH — resolved EARLY, and the criteria contained TWO of my own errors, corrected here. WHAT HAPPENED (primary: Federal Register 91 FR 49426, FR Doc 2026-15779, FERC Secretary's notice dated 7/30, filed 8/3, published 8/4): on 2026-07-28 PJM AND the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners EACH filed a Rule 212 motion to hold the show-cause proceeding in abeyance for 90 DAYS. They asked FERC to shorten the answer period to five days (answers by 8/3); FERC did NOT grant that — the Secretary established answers due 5:00 p.m. ET Friday 2026-08-07. FERC has NOT yet ruled on the motions themselves. ⚠️ ERROR 1 — WRONG DOCKET: the large-load show cause is EL26-67-000, NOT EL25-49. EL25-49 (with EL25-49-002, AD24-11-001, EL25-20-001, ER26-1479-000) is the EARLIER CO-LOCATION proceeding (Constellation complaint, 12/18/2025 order, separately modified 6/18/2026). I fused two proceedings. ⚠️ ERROR 2 — WRONG DIRECTIVE COUNT: the PJM order carries a FOUR-item directive list and OMITS the standalone co-location directive found in the four 'template' orders — FERC limited the PJM order to large loads NOT co-located with generation. So 'across FERC's 5 directed areas' was never the right test for THIS docket. ⚠️ THE SUBSTANTIVE QUESTION IS DEFERRED, NOT ANSWERED: the registered alternative path fired on time, but 'concrete reform vs bare justification' is unresolved — successor registered as WATT-09. If FERC grants, the 8/17 response deadline moves ~90 days to roughly mid-November 2026.
